Hi everyone, I'm a postdoc at the University of Michigan. I mostly study Hodge theory as it relates to algebraic geometry (D-modules, perverse sheaves, mixed Hodge modules, etc.). I'm interested in formalizing these theories although to me it seems that this is a long way away, so I'd be happy to contribute to projects which work toward making this possible. So I guess this would be anything involving for example (sheaf) cohomology, basic Hodge theory, derived categories, complex analytic and algebraic varieties, as well as many other things.

I'm still very new to Lean but I'm getting better. Right now I'm mostly intimidated by starting to contribute to mathlib and getting to know how everything is implemented. It's also unclear to me where exactly I should start. Does anyone know what the state of Hodge theory in Lean is and what is being worked on or needs to be worked on? Any general tips for a first-time contributer are also greatly appreciated. If you're actively working on things of this nature then I'd also be open to chatting directly.

As far as I know, there is no Hodge theory in mathlib, but there is some AI-generated theory in Tau Ceti. There was a recent discussion about this here: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/116395-maths/topic/Hodge.20structure.20and.20maybe.20Shimura.20varieties/with/618995566
Also here #Formal conjectures > Coordination for the Hodge Conjecture formalisation @ 💬

Should I understand that this means there is no desire to formalize Hodge theory in mathlib, since there is already work done in Tau Ceti and in this Hodge conjecture formalization? I wanted to do this to gain experience working with Lean but I'm also interested in contributing to some community project, so if I could do both at the same time that would be nice. I'm not very interested in generating a bunch of AI code and checking that it works.
No, even if something is already in Tau Ceti one can add it to mathlib. On the other hand the process can be much slower, but you will learn more things about how formalization works.
